headline: A preprint reports that retrieving long simulator output can divert agents from authoritative evidence
summary: In an Oct 19 arXiv preprint, authors report that how tool results are delivered changed answer accuracy in PHREEQC agent tasks. Across 158 execution-verified multiple-choice items, table-of-contents retrieval rather than inline report delivery was associated with an 11.3-point drop for GPT-5.1; GPT-5.2’s reported 7.9-point drop was not significant after Holm correction. Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4 showed no detectable net effect. The authors traced some errors to agents answering from higher-precision output files instead of the simulator report, and report that naming the authoritative report improved results in intervention runs. These are author-reported results in one deterministic scientific simulator, not an independent reproduction or evidence of a general retrieval penalty.
